Vernal Hanging-Parrot

पिचू पोपट

Loriculus vernalis

The Vernal Hanging-Parrot is a tiny green parrot with a short tail and a bright red rump. It moves actively among leaves, flowers and fruit, where its green plumage can make it much easier to hear than to see.

About the bird

How to recognise the Vernal Hanging-Parrot

Its small size and short tail give it a very different shape from the larger parakeets. A red rump is an important field mark, while males also show a blue patch on the throat.

These birds climb and reach around branches as they feed. They belong to the hanging-parrot group, which is known for resting upside down.

Natural habitat

The places where it lives

It uses forest, woodland, plantations and well-wooded gardens. Fruiting and flowering trees are especially important because they provide much of its food.

A bird may remain in the leafy canopy while feeding, then move quickly between trees. Local movements often follow changes in the supply of fruits and blossoms.

Food habits

What it eats and how it feeds

Soft fruits and berries, including figs, are important foods. It also feeds on seeds, buds and blossoms, and takes nectar from flowers.

Its climbing ability allows it to reach food from many angles. Rather than staying at one feeding site throughout the year, it may move as different trees come into fruit or flower.

Where it occurs in India

Where you may find it in India

The Vernal Hanging-Parrot occurs in the Western Ghats and associated wooded regions of peninsular India. It is also found in parts of the eastern Himalayan foothills and northeastern India.

Wooded areas in Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, Kerala and Tamil Nadu are among the regions where it can be encountered. Even within its range, the availability of feeding trees strongly influences where it is seen.
